data.title: Tesla’s new Automatic Collision Evasion can turn on FSD to avoid a crash [2026.27.5]
data.description:
Tesla is preparing to roll out a new safety feature that can automatically turn on Full Self-Driving (FSD) when the vehicle determines the driver may not react to an imminent collision.

The new features is called Automatic Collision Evasion, and appears in release notes for software update 2026.27.5, which also includes FSD (Supervised) v14.3.9. The update has not yet been released to the public and is currently being tested internally by Tesla employees. We are unable to share the original screenshot of the release notes as it contains an employee’s VIN.

However, according to the release notes we were able to see, the feature is designed to engage while the vehicle is being driven manually. Importantly, since it is tied to FSD, it will only be available on cars with a FSD license or subscription.

“Automatic Collision Evasion activates Full Self-Driving (Supervised) to keep your vehicle safe and then continue driving. It can engage while you are driving manually and detects that you are not sufficiently attentive to the road (for example, reaching toward the back seat), or that Full Self-Driving (Supervised) may have been unintentionally disengaged.”

The description suggests the feature goes beyond Tesla’s existing Automatic Emergency Braking and collision avoidance systems. Rather than simply applying the brakes or making a short evasive steering manoeuvre, Automatic Collision Evasion can activate FSD to take control and continue driving after avoiding the immediate danger.

Tesla also appears to be combining information from its exterior cameras with the cabin camera. The latter is already used for driver monitoring and can determine where the driver is looking, allowing the vehicle to recognize situations where the person behind the wheel may not be paying enough attention to respond.

Another notable part of the release notes is that Automatic Collision Evasion can intervene if FSD was unintentionally disengaged. Tesla doesn’t provide further details on what circumstances would qualify as an accidental disengagement.

The release notes also say owners should check the owner’s manual for more information, but the manuals have not yet been updated to include this new feature.

For now, the feature looks like it will be included with FSD v14.3.9 in software update 2026.27.5. As with any Tesla software release, wider public availability is unknown and if bugs are found during internal testing, its release could be delayed and not included in FSD v14.3.9.

data.title: Tesla Robotaxi fleet surpasses 1 million miles of unsupervised driving
data.description:
Tesla’s Robotaxi fleet has now surpassed 1 million miles (1.61 million km) of unsupervised driving, a major increase from the figure the company disclosed less than two months ago.

In its Q2 2026 update in July, Tesla said its fleet had accumulated more than 380,000 miles (about 612,000 km) of unsupervised operation. At the time, the figure drew considerable criticism as it came roughly a year after Tesla first launched its Robotaxi service, and about six months after it began fully autonomous operations.

Many also compared it to Waymo’s autonomous mileage count at over 200 million miles.

However, during Tesla’s Cybercab launch event in Austin on Thursday, Tesla’s head of AI, Ashok Elluswamy, revealed their figure has now jumped to more than 1 million miles (1.6 million km).

“As a testament to the safety I am happy to announce that we have achieved 1 million miles of unsupervised robo taxi operation,” Elluswamy said during the presentation.

The milestone means Tesla has added roughly 620,000 miles, or nearly 1 million kilometres, since the previous announcement in July. The cumulative total has increased by approximately 163%, reaching more than 2.6 times the earlier figure.

The company didn’t provide a city-by-city breakdown of its 1 million unsupervised miles, nor how much of the total was accumulated with Cybercab testing. Tesla currently operates driverless robotaxis in Austin, Dallas, Houston, Tampa, Miami, and Orlando.

With 1 million miles under their belt, that number should start climbing even faster for Tesla. Cybercab officially joined the Robotaxi fleet to select riders on Thursday, and Tesla says public Cybercab rides in Austin will begin Friday at 5 p.m. CT.

data.title: Tesla Reveals New Cybercab Details As It Officially Joins Robotaxi Fleet at 5pm Tonight
data.description:
Tesla held its Cybercab launch event in Austin yesterday, and while the company didn’t livestream the presentation, they did reveal lots of new details about the purpose-built robotaxi – everything from its efficiency and manufacturing process to the passenger experience.

One of the biggest new specifications is Cybercab’s aerodynamics. Tesla says the two-seater has a drag coefficient below 0.20, making it one of the most aerodynamic production vehicles ever developed. The company deliberately designed it for two passengers, saying more than 80% of rides involve two people or fewer.

Tesla also provided more details about what happens before a Cybercab even arrives. The Robotaxi network will search for nearby vehicles, including those currently completing another trip, and select whichever can reach the passenger fastest. Dynamic pricing will be used to balance supply and demand.

Once assigned, Cybercab will begin loading preferences stored in the rider’s Tesla account, automatically adjusting the temperature and seat position and restoring media accounts. A unique colour on the front light bar and interior lighting will help passengers identify their ride, while the Robotaxi app will display a compass pointing toward the correct vehicle.

Grok is integrated into Cybercab as well, accessible by voice, touchscreen or the app, with control over certain vehicle and ride functions. Tesla described the cabin as a “second living room” where passengers can watch videos, listen to music or work during a trip.

Accessibility was another major focus. Cybercab includes Braille on its doors and pull-over buttons, while the large butterfly doors provide a wider opening for passengers entering and exiting the vehicle. Tesla says it worked with disability groups and first responders during development.

Tesla also showed off Cybercab’s new Unboxed manufacturing process, which assembles separate vehicle modules rather than moving a completed body through a traditional production line. Tesla says the process reduces line size by 50% while allowing substantially higher output. The exterior panels use an injection-moulding process and recycled materials, eliminating the need for a conventional paint shop.

The event also brought a major milestone for Tesla’s broader autonomous program, with the company announcing its Robotaxi fleet has now accumulated more than 1 million miles of unsupervised driving.

Cybercab officially joined that fleet Thursday night to those who attended the event, and the next step won’t take long. Tesla says Cybercab rides will open to the public in Austin on Friday at 5 p.m. CT., although they didn’t specify how many Cybercabs will be available.

As we told you earlier this week, the company registered 45 units with the Texas DMV, so the fleet will likely only be that size, unless more are registered on Friday.

data.title: Another day, another Tesla driver ticketed for allegedly sleeping behind the wheel in B.C.
data.description:
If this story sounds familiar, it should. But no, this isn’t déjà vu. Yesterday we told you about how a Tesla driver had been fined for allegedly sleeping behind the wheel on Highway 1 in North Vancouver.

Today, police have released video of yet another incident. This time it happened on August 27 at around 7:45 a.m., during the morning rush hour on Highway 1 near 248 Street in Langley.

According to B.C. Highway Patrol, an officer was travelling to a priority call when he passed a Tesla and noticed the man behind the wheel with his eyes closed and both hands off the steering wheel.

The officer diverted from the original call and pulled the Tesla over.

“The police officer’s observations and his Body Worn Camera appeared to show the Tesla driver was asleep, though the driver claimed otherwise,” said Sergeant Michael McLaughlin with BC Highway Patrol. “This traffic stop took a valuable resource away from another police call. If drivers would stop sleeping behind the wheel, we could go help people who need us more.”

The driver was handed a $368 ticket for driving without due care and attention, along with an $81 fine for failing to produce a driver’s licence.

Other officers were ultimately able to respond to the original call, which involved a man with an extensive police history walking on the highway.

This is now the fifth separate incident involving an allegedly inattentive Tesla driver reported in B.C. this year.

In March, a Model Y driver was ticketed after allegedly appearing asleep on Highway 1 in Coquitlam. A West Kelowna driver was then caught reading documents while using Full Self-Driving (FSD) in July. That same month, another driver was filmed apparently asleep between Golden and Revelstoke.

Then on Wednesday, police revealed a fourth incident in which witnesses recorded a Tesla driver allegedly asleep on Highway 1 in North Vancouver on August 11.

Not to sound like a broken record, but Tesla’s FSD (and Autopilot) is a Level 2 driver-assistance system. Regardless of how capable the technology may be, the driver remains responsible for staying awake, attentive and ready to take control.

data.title: Tesla Tops South Korea Import Sales for Seventh Straight Month
data.description:
Tesla held the lead in South Korea sales of imported cars for a seventh straight month in August, with the Model Y outselling every passenger vehicle in the country.

According to the Korea Automobile Importers & Distributors Association (KAIDA), Tesla registered 10,400 vehicles last month, more than BMW (6,180) and Mercedes-Benz (4,037) combined. It was the third time this year Tesla has beaten the two German brands together, after April and May.

With that success, Tesla’s share of imported passenger cars rose to 34.9%, volume was up 30.4% from a year earlier, and claimed its sixth straight month above 10,000 registrations.

The Model Y accounted for 9,638 of those, about a third of every imported car registered in the country in August. The Model Y Premium led all imported models with 7,490, followed by 1,746 Model Y L and 402 Model Y Premium Long Range units.

That was enough to beat Kia’s Sorento, the top domestic model, which posted 6,397 registrations. The 3,241-unit gap is the widest of three months this year the Model Y has led the overall sales chart, after May and July.

As we previously reported, the Model Y returned to the top in July with 8,705 registrations, just ahead of the Hyundai Grandeur. Tesla first took the import lead in the first quarter with 20,964 deliveries, then set a monthly record in April at 13,190 vehicles.

Through August, Tesla has registered 76,776 vehicles in South Korea, up 122.3% from 34,543 a year earlier. The Model Y’s 61,702 year-to-date total sits 6,274 behind the Sorento with four months left.

data.title: New Tesla Cybercab Rider Guide reveals emergency stop system, cabin monitoring, and more
data.description:
Just hours before the Cybercab launch event is expected to begin, Tesla has published a new Rider Guide. The guide gives us our first look at how passengers will interact with the purpose-built robotaxi, including what happens when something goes wrong.

Unsurprisingly, the guide confirms Cybercab has just two seats and no steering wheel, accelerator pedal, or brake pedal. Riders instead control their trip through the central touchscreen and Tesla’s Robotaxi app.

However, one of the more interesting details is Cybercab’s emergency stop system. A physical Stop button located between the overhead dome lights can be pressed to initiate an immediate pull-over request. Doing so also ends the ride and connects the passenger with Tesla Robotaxi Support.

Passengers can also ask Cybercab to pull over using either the touchscreen or Robotaxi app. The vehicle will find a safe place to stop, although Tesla says that it may take longer to do so while travelling on a highway.

For more serious situations, if a rider believes they are in immediate danger, they can fully pull the mechanical door release. Doing so ends the trip and tells Cybercab to stop in its lane as soon as it can safely do so. If the vehicle is travelling at highway speeds, it may pull over instead of stopping in the lane.

The guide also explains how Tesla will keep an eye on what is happening inside the Cybercab. A cabin camera can detect whether the vehicle is occupied and can also be used if a rider needs help during an emergency. Cybercab’s microphone can send audio to Tesla when a passenger contacts support or when the vehicle detects a safety-related event.

After passengers leave, the cabin camera can even check whether the Cybercab is clean and whether any belongings were left behind before its next trip.

Other details include automatic doors that recognize the ride requester’s phone, a 20.2-cubic-foot rear trunk, and a restriction preventing children under 13 from riding in Cybercab for now.

You can read the full guide below.

data.title: Tesla generated over half a billion dollars from SpaceX and xAI in 2025
data.description:
Elon Musk’s companies are known to do business with one another. According to a company filing, Tesla accrued up to $573 million in revenue from SpaceX and xAI alone in 2025.

The original 2025 annual filing stated that most of the income (about $430 million) came from xAI, which is Musk’s AI-focused company. Later, in an amended filing, Tesla reported an additional $143.3 million in proceeds from SpaceX.

SpaceX is one of the biggest buyers of the Cybertruck. The space exploration company has been swapping its gas-powered trucks for battery-powered units since October 2025. By purchasing the electric truck from its sister company, SpaceX has been helping to prop up the stainless-steel automobile.

Bloomberg, citing new vehicle registration data for the last quarter of 2025, reported that SpaceX bought 1,279 Cybertrucks from Tesla. This purchase represented more than 18 percent of US sales in that quarter and was worth more than $100 million.

Analysts estimate that Musk-affiliated entities bought more than 200 Cybertrucks in the first two months of 2026.

Other instances of business dealings between Musk’s companies include xAI procuring Megapack energy storage batteries from Tesla. The EV maker’s latest filing revealed that more than $78 million in revenue came from xAI as of February 2026.

Tesla has integrated xAI’s Grok chatbot in its vehicles. Meanwhile, X incorporated the chatbot on its social media platform before being absorbed by the AI company in March 2025. Blurring the lines even further, SpaceX recently acquired xAI, and the resulting behemoth is planning to launch the biggest initial public offering (IPO) later in 2026.

SpaceX is also jointly producing chips with Tesla.

data.title: Tesla pulled the plug on Cybertruck RWD after selling just 173 trucks
data.description:
It is no secret that the Tesla Cybertruck is not selling as fast as the company wanted. However, just how poor sales were for the Rear-Wheel Drive (RWD) version before it was discontinued have been revealed by a recent recall action.

Earlier this week we reported that Tesla was recalling the Cybertruck. According to Tesla, stud holes in the brake rotors may crack, especially under intense use such as rough roads or sharp turns. This could cause the wheel stud to detach from the hub, potentially leading to a crash.

Tesla claims there has been no accident or injuries traceable to the potential fault. However, the interesting part of the recall process is the number of units involved.

According to the documentation, the brake problem affects Cybertrucks of a specific configuration: the RWD version, which Tesla released about a year ago, before discontinuing it due to what was believed to be low sales. Tesla does not state the number of Cybertrucks delivered in quarterly reports. The figure is usually lumped with “other models”, which includes the soon-to-be-discontinued Model S and Model X.

The recall notice states that only 173 Cybertrucks need to be brought in, meaning the company only sold 173 units of this variant.

The model, which cost about $10,000 less than the base All-Wheel Drive (AWD) but lacked many of the core features, was meant to be the affordable Cybertruck. Selling only 173 units for the configuration is a poor record for an electric vehicle with as much visibility. It is no wonder that Tesla has discontinued sales of the version after just a few months.

data.title: California makes big changes to autonomous vehicle legislation
data.description:
The State of California has made significant changes to the autonomous vehicle landscape through Assembly Bill No. 1777.

The first is that state lawmakers have closed a loophole that prevented driverless vehicles from being issued citations. The previous legislation stated that the person behind the wheel would be liable for a violation, but officers could not issue a ticket to a driverless vehicle. Now, a robotaxi can be issued a notice of non-compliance, and the manufacturer will be responsible for paying the ticket.

To keep companies responsible, the new law will force manufacturers to report the citation within 72 hours. Failure to do so empowers the California Department of Motor Vehicles to impose stricter sanctions, including capping fleet sizes and suspending permits for repeat offenders.

In addition, lawmakers have given first responders greater control over robotaxis, allowing them to move vehicles obstructing fire and rescue operations. The legislation requires vehicles to respond to first responders’ commands and will use a variety of tech to do so, including geofencing to prevent driverless vehicles from approaching live operations.

The other major change that lawmakers made is that the state has lifted the ban on heavy-duty autonomous trucks. To be road-certified, vehicles weighing more than 10,001 lbs and medium-sized trucks weighing over 14,001 pounds will need to undergo 500,000 miles of testing with a human driver on board. Once completed, the vehicles can then move to fully driverless operations.

data.title: Tesla Model 3 Prices in Canada Slashed, Now Starting at $39,490
data.description:
Tesla has made a significant move in Canada, reopening orders for the Model 3 with dramatically reduced pricing.

The low prices are thanks to Tesla shifting its supply strategy and now importing Model 3 units from Giga Shanghai.

The headline grabber is the Model 3 Premium Rear-Wheel Drive (RWD), which starts at just $39,490.

That price positions it as one of the most affordable EVs, especially considering its 463 km of range and 4.2s sprint to 100km/h.

However, because these vehicles are built in China, they do not qualify for Canada’s federal EVAP rebate program.

It is worth reiterating this is the Premium variant, and not the stripped-down Standard version of the electric sedan Tesla introduced last year.

At the other end of the lineup, the Model 3 Performance is now listed at $74,990. Previously this variant was priced at $89,990 when it was sourced from the U.S. and subject to tariffs.

With the update, Tesla has also removed the Premium Long Range Model 3 from its lineup in Canada. Previously this vehicle was priced at $79,990 before it was removed.

Buyers won’t have to wait long with the first customer deliveries expected as early as May or June.

The return of Shanghai-built units comes after Tesla faced challenges selling U.S.-built vehicles in Canada with inflated prices due to tariffs. By pivoting back to China production—something it has done before—Tesla is once again able to maintain supply while keeping prices in check.

For Canadian buyers, the timing couldn’t be better. With rising fuel prices and renewed interest in electric vehicles, a sub-$40,000 Model 3—even without incentives—could drive strong demand. The Premium RWD is a high-value option for buyers looking to enter the Tesla ecosystem without stretching into higher trims.
